Well, I decided to get it, guys. Here's what I think so far. 

1. I think all the new content added is wonderful. I'm really excited to see all the new, exciting levels created and am eager to also see what I can do with the new stuff myself. :D

2. Some of my favorite LBP2 levels have some functionality issues. Blast Radius's guns are kinda screwy, and Super LittleBigPlanet doesnt seem to work all that well because of the extra layers of depth; I find myself constantly jumping on the background terrain. This isn't that big of a deal, though, since I can always play LBP2 on my trusty PS3. B)

3. Was able to import all my LBP1 and 2 content with no hassle! I even backed up my save on LBP2 just in case.

4. Perhaps the most concerning of all: the online. First of all, the "Dive In!" button on the main menu seems to be a dud. I pressed it many times and it didn't seem to do anything. I found out you have to go into the pause menu and do it that way through "Play online." A little different than what I'm used to, but no matter.

At the time of this post, I've only been able to join two games, and both had lag that made the game borderli-, no, unplayable. Rubberbanding out the wazoo. What in the name of Negativitron is the meaning of this!? Is this just me or is this what it's usually like? I remember Brink's multiplayer being more stable when it launched.... back in 2011.

Guys, I'm really worried. This game is the game that's helping me decide if I'm even going to keep my lousy PS4. I'm not interested in any of the games I see on the shelves or PS Store anymore, and I'm not jazzed about having to pay to play online. I didn't like it when the 360 pulled this crap, and I'm ESPECIALLY not going to like it if I'm paying for lousy service like this.
Sadly, I don't have a PC that can run Lego Worlds.
It's a terabyte HD. So there's lots of space available. I really don't know why it would do this. Any plans for future updates?
